prompt: When you open a pull request from a fork back to an upstream repository, what actually triggers the CI pipeline defined in a GitHub Actions workflow?
choices: A maintainer manually clicking 'Run checks' after reviewing the diff
GitHub firing a pull_request event that any workflow watching for it picks up automatically
The act of forking the repository, which runs CI once immediately
Merging the PR into the base branch

prompt: In a required_status_checks branch protection rule, what does setting "strict": true actually enforce?
choices: Only repo admins can bypass failing checks
Every commit author must have 2FA enabled
The branch must be up to date with the base branch before an existing passing check result is considered valid
Status checks must complete in under 5 minutes or they count as failed

prompt: A repo renames a CI job from `test` to `build-and-test` in its workflow YAML but the branch protection rule's required_status_checks.contexts still lists `test`. What happens to new PRs against the protected branch?
choices: GitHub automatically updates the required context name to match
The merge button stays blocked forever because the required context `test` never reports again
Branch protection is disabled automatically until the mismatch is fixed
CI simply runs both the old and new job names

prompt: What does enforce_admins: true in a branch protection rule mean in practice?
choices: Only admins are allowed to approve pull requests
Admins get an extra required review step that other contributors don't
Even repository admins cannot merge past failing or pending required status checks
Admins must enable two-factor authentication before pushing

prompt: Writing "Fixes #152" in a pull request description that gets merged into the default branch causes what to happen automatically?
choices: Nothing — it is purely a documentation convention with no functional effect
GitHub closes issue #152 and the linked project board moves it to its closed-state column
Issue #152 is deleted from the repository
A new branch protection rule is created referencing issue #152

prompt: Which of these is the strongest example of a good first infra/tooling-adjacent pull request to an unfamiliar open-source repo?
choices: A large refactor of the build system reorganizing how all CI jobs are structured
A one-line reformatting change with no linked issue and no explanation of why it's needed
A fix for a flaky CI step, including the failing run's log link and the passing run after the fix
Renaming variables throughout the codebase to match the contributor's preferred style

prompt: You run gh pr merge 47 --merge and get: "Required status checks: build-and-test (pending), security-scan (failing)". What does this indicate about the underlying mechanism?
choices: GitHub is only issuing a warning; the merge will proceed after a 10-second delay
GitHub's server-side merge operation itself is refusing the request because contexts listed in required_status_checks have not all reported success
The PR reviewer rejected the change, which GitHub is reporting as a check failure
The repository has run out of CI minutes for the billing period
